newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS WINS, IVANISEVIC OUSTED IN INDIANAPOLIS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS WINS, IVANISEVIC OUSTED IN INDIANAPOLIS.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras claimed a solid if unspectacular victory in the second round of the $1 millon RCA Championships Wednesday but lethargic second seed Goran Ivanisevic was ambushed by a determined Australian outsider.
Sampras, the top seed, saddled Australia with its only loss on the day from five matches as he ousted world number 585 qualifier Josh Eagle 6-3 7-5 in just over an hour.
The other four players from Down Under rolled past the opposition on a cloudy day at the Indianapolis Tennis Center.
Unseeded Jason Stoltenberg, a 1996 Wimbledon semifinalist, led the charge, fighting back after standing a set and 4-1 down on Wednesday after an overnight rain interruption against Ivanisevic.
The world number 60 ended his knockout of the big-serving Croatian world number three with a barrage of four consecutive aces.
"I don't know where those came from," Stoltenberg said of the rockets he uncorked to get out of trouble on the way back from love-40 in the tenth game of the final set.
"I figured I'd been pushing my serve all day and I was down. I threw it up and hit it and reeled off four. I just picked my spot, relaxed and hit the serve. I was just lucky I hit four great ones."
Ivanisevic, known for inconsistent play, blamed a poor year. "I haven't had a very good past few months," he said. "I was terrible at the French Open and Wimbledon. My confidence is low."

The other Aussie success stories were seventh seed Todd Woodbridge and non-seeds Mark Woodforde and Richard Fromberg. Woodbridge beat Czech Martin Damm 6-7 (6-8) 7-5 7-5, Woodforde eliminated 12th-seeded Canadian Open champion Chris Woodruff 6-3 6-3 and Fromberg defeated American Mark Merklein 6-3 7-6 (7/1).
Of a dozen seeds on court Wednesday, all but three advanced to the third round. Cedric Pioline, the eighth seed, was ambushed by Soth African Grant Stafford 2-6 6-4 6-4.
Andre Agassi won his second match in a row as his comeback from a world ranking of 74 continued. The 14th seed was pleased with his steady progress.
"It's a catch-22," said the former world number one. "You need confidence to win matches and you need to win matches to gain confidence."
Sampras was relatively untroubled by Eagle, better known for his doubles prowess. The top seed is tuning up for the U.S. Open and could claim his sixth title of the season if he wins here.
"The first match of the week is always tough," said Sampras. They are using diffenet balls here than last weekend (when he won the title in Cincinnati). It took me a while to get used to them.
"It's always nice to get the first match out of the way. But I will put last week behind and move on. It's good to be playing this well so close to the U.S. Open."
